neighbours.label: ' on', or a verb or noun leading to it, when something physically rests on a surface (sleeps on, perched on, standing on, his foot on)
fire: The cat naps on a cushion near the window every day.
An owl perched on the fence behind the old barn.
He pinned the snake by pressing his boot on its neck.
A child standing on a chair could reach the top shelf.
Pigeons roost on the ledge above our front door.
She set her heavy bag down on the kitchen table.
The goat stood on the roof of the small shed.
A parrot sat on the sailor's shoulder all afternoon.
quiet: The cat relies on a neighbor near the window every day.
An owl was on the news behind the old anchor.
He spent money by going on a trip around its coast.
A child working on a project could reach the top score.
Pigeons carry on the tradition above all others.
She kept her sister on the phone at the kitchen table.
The goat went on to win at the small fair.
A parrot carried on talking to the sailor all afternoon.

notes: Card: ' on' x14, 'ched' x4, ' foot' x2, ' in', ' them', ' feet', with animals perched, sleeping and standing. Probes: 'sleeps on a gurney' 0.788, 'placing his foot' 0.781, 'standing on a desk' 0.629, 'perched' 0.616; 'depends on a gift' 0.066, 'went on a trip' 0.019. Near misses keep ' on' in abstract and phrasal senses.
